name: V. Investment Policies (b) — Issuer Concentration
text: The Fund cannot Invest more than 5% Of fts assets at the time of purchase in obligations of any one issuer, except for obligations Issued or guaranteed by the U. S. Government, Its. agencies and instrumentalities or repurchase ‘agreements collateralized by such obligations.

name: V. Investment Policies (b) — Variable Rate Limit
text: The Fund may not invest more than 35% of Its total assets at the time of purchase in variable rate securities.

name: V. Investment Policies (b) — Illiquid Securities Limit
text: A maximum of 15% of the Fund's total assets may be Invested in illiquid securities as that term is defined in the SEC's Rule 2a-7,

name: V. Investment Policies (b) — Private Placement Liquidity
text: Private placement obligations (e.g. Rule 144A Securities) will generally be considered iquid unless at least two broker/dealers provide an active secondary market (trade date plus three business days settlement, market bid quotations)..

name: V. Investment Policies (b) — Overnight Maturity
text: At least 20% of the Fund’s total assets will be Invested in assets scheduled to mature overnight,

name: V. Investment Policies (c) Portfolio Maturity — Average Maturity
text: (c) Portfolio Maturity The maximum dollar-weighted average maturity of the Trust‘s portfolio will be 90 days.

name: V. Investment Policies (c) — Maturity Calculation
text: For purposes of determining the dollar-weighted average maturity of the Trust’s portfollo, the maturity of any obligation is deemed to be the shortest of the following: (i) the stated maturity date of the obligation; (if) the next Interest rate reset for variable rate obligations: or (ii) the next put exercise date {for obligations - with put features), However, for purposes of determining the maturity of a variable rate demand obligation, the maturity is deemed to be equal to the longer of the period of time remaining until the next readjustment of the Interest rate or the period of time remaining unt# the principal amount can be recovered from the issuer on demand.

name: V. Investment Policies (d) Maturity of Portfolla Instruments — Maximum Maturity
text: (d) Maturity of Portfolla Instruments The maximum maturity of a security shall be five years.

name: V. Investment Policies (d) — Variable and Floating Rate Maturity
text: For purposes of determining the maturity of variable and floating rate obligations, the shorter of the period remalning until the next adjustment of the Interest rate or the period remaining until the principal amount can be recovered through demand will be used.

name: V. Investment Policies (d) — Repurchase Agreement Maturity
text: Repurchase agreements shall mature In one year or less.

name: V. Investment Policies (d) — Repurchase Agreement End Date
text: For purposes of determining the maturity of obligations subject to repurchase agreements the end date of the agreement, and not the maturities of the underlying obligation are utilized,

name: VI. Risk Factors — Investment Value
text: VI. RISK FACTORS The value of the Shares witl change with the change in value of the Trust's investments. Many factors can affect those values,

name: VI. Risk Factors — Credit Risk
text: Because the Trust Invests in debt securities, such as notes and bonds, the Trust Is subject to credit risk and interest rate risk. If the issuer or guarantor of a debt security or the counterparty to a derivative or repurchase agreement is unable or unwilling to make timely principal and/or Interest payments or to otherwise honor its obligations, the value of the related debt security may decline. Debt securities are consequently subject to varying degrees of credit risk, which Is often reflected In the credit rating given to a particular security.

name: VI. Risk Factors — Interest Rate Risk
text: interest rate risk is the risk that Interest rates may increase, which would reduce the resale value of the securitles held by the Trust (Including any Investments In U.S, Government obligations). Those debt securities with longer durations tend to be more sensitive to changes In Interest rates, usually making them more volatile in value than securities with shorter durations. In 6 of 12 .
